security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, defensive reference material, and public documentation links. Confirmed issues remain in supply chain guidance: an unverified curl-to-bash installer, a mutable binary download, plaintext credential examples, and a mutable CI action reference.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the tool version, download a release artifact, verify checksum or signature, and run the installer explicitly.

remediation.issue: Cosign installation uses a latest URL without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use a package manager or pin a release version and verify the downloaded binary before installation.

remediation.issue: Registry credentials are shown in plaintext Syft configuration examples.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer secret managers or CI secrets, and warn users not to commit configuration files containing credentials.

remediation.issue: The CI template uses a mutable GitHub Action branch reference.
remediation.suggestion: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs or reviewed release tags.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable SBOMs for vulnerability, license, and supply chain reviews. This skill guides Syft commands, output formats, CI integration, and attestation steps.
actual_capabilities: Plans Syft SBOM generation for container images, filesystems, and archives.
Recommends CycloneDX, SPDX, and syft-json formats for different toolchains.
Outlines CI/CD workflows for SBOM generation and artifact storage.
Explains SBOM signing and attestation steps with Cosign.
Helps review dependencies, licenses, and vulnerability scanning handoffs.
limitations: Requires Syft and related tools to be installed or available in containers.
May miss packages in unusual build systems or generated dependency files.
Does not replace vulnerability scanners, license counsel, or release approval.
Generated commands should be reviewed before use with private registries.

use_cases.title: Create Release SBOMs
use_cases.description: Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs for container images before release.

use_cases.title: Support Vulnerability Triage
use_cases.description: Produce Syft output that can feed Grype or another vulnerability scanner.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Document dependency inventories and signed SBOM artifacts for audit workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic SBOM
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one container image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Syft command plan to generate a CycloneDX SBOM for my container image. Include validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an SBOM Format
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CycloneDX, SPDX, and syft-json for my release process. Recommend one primary format and explain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Add SBOMs to CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow that generates, stores, and scans a Syft SBOM for every container release.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Attestation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a signed SBOM attestation process with Syft and Cosign. Include verification, storage, and access controls.

output_examples.input: Generate an SBOM for nginx:latest in CycloneDX format.
output: Recommended target: the container image nginx:latest.
Recommended format: CycloneDX JSON for broad scanner support.
Next steps: save the SBOM as a release artifact and scan it with your vulnerability tool.

output_examples.input: I need SBOM evidence for an audit.
output: Generate SBOMs for each released image and application archive.
Store the files with release metadata, build identifiers, and retention dates.
Sign production SBOMs and record verification results for audit review.

output_examples.input: Help me troubleshoot missing packages in a Syft SBOM.
output: Check whether package manager files are present in the scanned target.
Try all-layers scope for container images when packages appear in earlier layers.
Review exclusions before assuming Syft missed a dependency.

best_practices: Pin tool versions and verify downloaded installers before use in CI.
Store SBOMs with release metadata, access controls, and retention rules.
Regenerate and rescan SBOMs after dependency or base image changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat an SBOM as a complete vulnerability assessment.
Do not commit registry credentials or private package details in public repositories.
Do not publish SBOMs without reviewing sensitive internal package names.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create SBOM generation workflows with Syft for images, filesystems, archives, and CI pipelines.

faq.question: Which SBOM formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers CycloneDX JSON, CycloneDX XML, SPDX JSON, SPDX tag-value, syft-json, and text output.

faq.question: Can it scan an SBOM for vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can guide handoff to scanners such as Grype, but the scanner performs the vulnerability matching.

faq.question: Does it require Docker?
faq.answer: Docker is useful for container workflows, but local Syft can also scan filesystems and archives.

faq.question: Can it support compliance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps prepare dependency inventories, artifact records, and signed SBOM evidence for audits.

faq.question: Is this safe for private registries?
faq.answer: Yes, when credentials are handled through approved secret storage and generated commands are reviewed before use.
